_comment: Beats (docs/ADVENTURES.md §5.10, §8.6; game/story/beats.py): small scenes with pages and choices, played on the beat screen. when: conditions; choices: label, requires, check {skill, dc}, ops or success/failure, result lines.

text: The road leaves the fields here and goes on between banks of scrub, and at the bend you find it: {carcass}. The crows go up all at once.
You smell it before you see it. Off the road, in the ditch, {carcass}, and the flies thick over it.
There is a bend in the road where the scrub closes in, and it is there: {carcass}, and the ground round it torn up.
Whatever did this was not hungry. It ate the best of it and left the rest, as if to say it could.
Beyond the carcass the scrub is flattened in a wide swathe going off towards {home}.
Nothing on the road but you, and the wind in the scrub, and that smell.

label: Look closer.
result: You kneel by it. Whatever left this, you will know it again.

text: You go over the ground round the kill, a yard at a time: {track}.
Now you look properly. There is a story in the trampled ground, if you can read it: {track}.
The wounds first, then the ground: {track}, and blood on the scrub at a man's height.

label: Read the tracks, however long it takes.
result: It is big, bigger than anything that should live in {area}, and it went back up towards {home} by a way the herders do not use.
fail_result: It takes you half the day, and a good deal of swearing, but in the end the ground tells you: it is big, and it went up towards {home}.

label: Take a tooth from the carcass, broken off in the wound. Proof for {town}.
result: The tooth is as long as your finger and yellow with age. {town} will believe you now.

label: Burn the carcass, so it draws nothing else down from {home}.
result: The smoke goes up black and greasy. Whatever watches from the hills will know someone is here, and is not afraid.

text: You know what it fears now. What is left is to bring it to you, or to go to it.
There are two ways to hunt a beast like {villain}: make it come to you, or follow it until it turns. Both have killed better hunters than you.
{ally} lays it out plainly. "Stake out bait and wait, or follow its trail till it turns. Your choice. I know which one I'd pick, and I'm not telling you."

label: Stake out a bait here, and wait in the dark.
result: The night is long and cold and nothing comes, and nothing, and then the bait is gone and {villain_short} is among you.

label: Follow its trail, and let it turn on you.
result: The trail goes on through the scrub and the broken ground, and then there is no more trail, because {villain_short} has stopped running.

text: {home} gapes in the hillside. Nothing grows near the mouth of it, and the bones there are not all sheep.
You reach {home} with the wind in your face, which is the only luck you have had. The den's mouth breathes out a warm stink.
Here it is: {home}. Below the mouth, a midden of bones and wool, and a path worn smooth by something heavy coming and going.

label: Go in quietly, keeping to the walls.
result: You go in as quiet as breath. If it sleeps, it will wake to you standing over it.
fail_result: A stone turns under your boot and rattles away into the dark. Somewhere below, something stops breathing to listen.

label: Light a fire at the mouth and let the smoke go in first.
result: The smoke rolls into the den. From somewhere deep comes the sound of something heavy moving, and then a noise like no animal you know.

label: Go in with everything you have, and let it know you are coming.
result: You go in shouting. Let it come. You are done with waiting.

text: {omen}
You stop on the way, and look, and wish you had not. {omen}
{omen} Nobody else on the road seems to have seen it, or they will not say.
You go on, but you go on faster.
It is a long way yet to anywhere with a door that bars.
{villain_short} is not far. It wants you to know that.
In the morning there is a dead hind at the edge of your camp, laid out as neat as a gift, its throat torn out.
At first light you find it: a sheep's head, set on a stone where the fire was, watching the camp.
Something came in the night, and went, and left you a carcass at the edge of the firelight. Nobody heard a thing.
It knows where you sleep. It wants you to know it knows.
{villain_short} does not need to write letters.
The message is plain enough: it is not afraid of you.

label: Burn it, and break camp.
result: You burn it, and go, and keep looking back.

label: Study it: how it was killed tells you something.
result: The bite is the bite of the old songs. You learn a little of how it kills.
fail_result: It tells you nothing you did not know, except that it was very strong.

text: In the dead of night the horses scream, and then there is something huge between the fire and the dark.
The watch shouts once, and you wake to a weight hitting the edge of camp and a smell like a slaughterhouse.
It comes in the black hour before dawn, testing: a rush at the firelight, and then gone, and then a rush from the other side.

label: Stand to the fire and drive it off.
result: You stand, and shout, and swing, and it goes. It was only testing you.
fail_result: It knocks you down on its way out of the light, and is gone before you are up.

label: Throw it the meat you carry, and let it go.
result: It takes the meat and goes. You have taught it something, and you are not sure what.

text: You come back to the kill to look again, now that you know what you are looking for.
The kill is older now, and the crows have done their work, but there is more here to read.
The bones of the kill tell their story to anyone who knows the beasts of {area}.

label: Think back on every beast-tale you know.
fail_result: Nothing comes. You will have to ask someone who knows.

title: {villain}
text: {hook}
Word is going round, and it is all the same word: {hook}
{hook} Everyone you meet seems to be talking of nothing else.

label: I will hunt it. (A tale begins: the journal keeps it.)
Not now.
result: Someone else, then. Or no one. You put it out of your mind, almost.
